item.title: Gross GST collections rise 23% to ₹2.31 trillion in October on strong sales
item.description: Gross GST collections increased 23 per cent to over Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday. Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16 per cent to over Rs 1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42 per cent to Rs 72,246 crore. The Rs 2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of Rs 51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over Rs 1.37 lakh crore, data showed. Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 27,934 crore in October. After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26 per cent to over Rs 2.03 lakh crore in October. During April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2 per cent to over Rs 14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13 per cent to over Rs 12.69 lakh crore.

item.title: Commercial LPG rates increase by ₹10, ATF prices up by ₹1.37 per litre
item.description: Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices rose by Rs 1.37 per litre from Sunday, and commercial LPG rates increased by Rs 10 per 19-kg cylinder in step with firming international benchmarks, according to state-owned oil firms. ATF prices were increased to Rs 138.50 per litre from Rs 137.12 per litre. This is the fourth straight monthly increase in jet fuel (ATF) prices, necessitated by firming rates of international benchmarks. Prices were last raised by a steep Rs 16 a litre on October 1. Prior to that, ATF prices were hiked by Rs 6.28 per litre on September 1 and by Rs 5 a litre on August 1. Jet fuel accounts for up to 40 per cent of the operating cost of airlines, and the price hike will further push up carrier expenditure. Alongside, rates of commercial LPG - cooking gas used in hotels and restaurants - were hiked by Rs 10 per 19-kg cylinder to Rs 2,820, according to the oil companies. item.title: Record oil imports reflect strong refinery runs, flexible Russian buying
item.description: India's crude oil imports surged to a record high of about 5.6 million barrels per day in October, with refiners stepping up purchases from the Middle East and Russia despite ongoing geopolitical tensions, according to data from energy intelligence firm Kpler. Middle Eastern supplies accounted for about 2.3 million barrels per day, and Russian crude flows remained strong at around 2 million bpd, Kpler lead analyst Nikhil Dubey said in a post. Higher ship-to-ship transfers helped move more crude through the Strait of Hormuz, supporting a recovery in Gulf supplies during September and October and giving Indian refiners greater flexibility in sourcing. Russian shipments could moderate in November and December as attacks in the Black Sea push up freight rates, making those barrels less competitive on a landed-cost basis. item.title: Centre releases addl instalment of tax devolution of ₹1.09 trn to states
item.description: The Centre on Saturday released additional instalment of tax devolution to state governments totalling over Rs 1.09 lakh crore. This is in addition to the regular monthly devolution and the second additional instalment this financial year. The Union government released tax devolution of Rs 1,09,019 crore to state governments, the finance ministry said in a statement. "This release is in view of the upcoming festive season and to enable states to accelerate capital spending, and also to finance their development/welfare related expenditure," the ministry said. Currently, 41 per cent of taxes collected by the Centre is devolved in 14 instalments among states during a fiscal year.

item.title: GST reforms from Nov 1: Faster refunds, easier registration for sellers
item.description: Simplified GST registration for small sellers on e-commerce platforms, unified documentation for GST registration, faster refunds, and a Rs 10,000 threshold for issuing GST notices are some of the Goods and Services Tax process reforms that are likely to be rolled out from November 1, an official said on Thursday. The 57th GST Council meeting on October 8 approved a host of reforms in GST processes, primarily covering registration, returns, refund and adjudication. Officials said some of the changes approved by the Council that can be implemented through administrative processes will be brought into effect in phases from November 1, 2026. The changes which require an amendment to the GST law would be implemented from April 1, 2027. The notifications and circulars on the relevant process reforms have already been approved by the legal department and are likely to be issued on Friday, an official said. item.title: Govt extends customs duty exemption on cotton imports up to Dec 31
item.description: Keeping in view raw material requirements of domestic textile industry, the Centre has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports until December 31, 2026, the textile ministry said on Saturday. The extension has been notified by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, dated October 30. Through this amendment, the existing exemption, which was available until October 2026, has been extended by two months, up to December 31, 2026. In May, the government had exempted cotton imports from customs duties for five months, till October 31, 2026.
